mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the previous 3 months signals inflationary pressure, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPI growth and subsequent 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month signals weakening economic conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE spikes and subsequent 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decline and subsequent 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous month signals strengthening supply-side conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO growth and subsequent 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) growth is below 1%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2 percentage points, it signals a tightening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increase and subsequent 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 0.5% signals a weakening supply chain, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between INDPRO decline and subsequent 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during late-cycle expansions.
